title: Wall-clock stamps must not create standalone user messages (operator directive)

payload.spec_source: operator live feedback 2026-09-24 16:10: "adding these empty user messages just for the timestamp is a little overdone. the idea was that the timestamp should be there, but dont put in a user message block just for timestamps sake"
payload.observed: Between-turn user messages containing only "[pragma wall-clock ...]" appear in the conversation (e.g. the 12:02:51 stamp visible in the operator TUI as a bare user turn) - the CLK-001 companion message after each tool-results batch.
payload.constraint: The model must still see the current wall clock each turn. CLK-001 documented why the stamp cannot ride INSIDE the tool-results message (a text part serializes before its tool results, breaking pairing) - so do NOT move it into the results message. Preferred mechanism: a per-request dynamic system block (like systemWithMCPStatus/systemWithHarnessManifest) carrying the current wall-clock, rebuilt each request; remove the companion user message entirely. Turn-budget/self-continue notices keep their existing first-line stamp inside real text appends.
payload.deliverables: RED test: tool-results batch followed by NO wall-clock user message AND next request system contains the stamp; GREEN with the system-block mechanism; adjacent: session files must not contain wall-clock-only user messages for NEW turns; full query suite; case record CLK-002 referencing this directive as spec source.

prior_attempt_note: attempt 1 died at ~80-turn cap mid multi-file change ($6.25, exit 1, partials discarded). Prior session 06f603fb has the analysis - the next worker may read its session transcript for salvageable design decisions. Scope discipline: (a) per-request system block carrying the stamp (new systemWithWallClock-style helper), (b) remove the companion user message + wall_clock_test update, (c) case record CLK-002 note. Land (a)+(b) with gates first.

title: Periodic model-based meta-observer: sample every live session tail every ~3min for waste patterns beyond mechanical invariants

payload.spec_source: operator 2026-09-24 16:14: "maybe we just dont have enough operational observability we will keep missing things, what about one watch for each of these every which check every couple of minutes... efficiency always requires meta observability"
payload.context: The wall-clock noise (CLK-002) was a value-level defect invisible to every current observer - only the operator caught it. Mechanical invariants (watcher alerts) cover countable failure; this adds the judging layer.
payload.design: A daemon (new mode of pragma-watch or a small sibling) that every ~3 minutes takes the tail of each live session event log and runs a CHEAP critic prompt over it: (1) what here is wasted motion (re-reads, stamp-noise, low-value turns, context growth per unit of progress)? (2) what is this session NOT checking that it should? (3) do any recent operator messages read as spec corrections that are not yet queue items? Findings auto-append to this queue with session+time provenance. Budget: one small model call per sample (~$0.02-0.10); at 3min cadence over 1-2 live sessions that is ~$0.5-2/hour - provider-budget bounded. Correlated-blind-spot caveat: same-model critics share blind spots; rotate --critic-model when available.
payload.deliverables: Implementation + tests + one live hour of recorded findings + report on what it caught that the mechanical watcher missed.

title: Threshold calibration: provider-tools system/tools estimate + zero-WindowConfig guard
worker_report: F8 estimate miscalibration confirmed for both modes: BuildCompactionDeps reserved EstimateSystemPromptTokens(PragmaLoopSystemPrompt) (~270 tokens) for every mode — provider-tools requests never carry that prompt (their fixed payload: custom + conversation system + MCP status + harness manifest + patch guidance + tool schemas, provider_tools_loop.go build sequence) and pragma requests carry custom + PragmaLoopSystemPrompt, so the custom prompt was missing there too; compact.ApplyResult replaces only Messages so the whole fixed payload is re-injected post-compaction and the reserve under-counted it. F8 zero-window confirmed mechanically: WindowConfig{} clamps AutoCompactThreshold to 0, ShouldAutoCompact true for every count when cooldown allows — compaction every MinTurnsCooldown; contradicts the CompactionDeps 'zero values disable' contract; no production caller passes zero today (all SetCompaction sites use BuildCompactionDeps, ctxWindow defaults 200_000) — latent API hazard, now guarded at the decision (ShouldAutoCompact rejects ContextWindow<=0) and at the wiring (BuildCompactionDeps ignores non-positive provider lookups). Boundary documented: configured small windows (googlevertex 8_192 → threshold 0) deliberately keep triggering — that every-cooldown case is open CMP-001.4b C-2, not F8; MCP tool schemas excluded from the reserve (ctx-dependent, dynamic) — the F6 trigger count includes them at decision time. Fix: compact/auto.go zero-window guard; query/engine.go EstimateCompactionReserve (mode-aware, mirrors each loop's request builder); BuildCompactionDeps uses it (nil-engine fallback = pragma-shape floor). RED on pre-fix tree (pre-drafted gates): ShouldAutoCompact(0, zero)=true; SystemPromptEst=270 vs floors 3000/1000. New composition gates RED vs the old estimation shape (270 vs 1003 tools+manifest/patch; 270 vs 1270 pragma) → GREEN. Adjacent: compact+query+cli -count=1 ok; query -race ok; orchestration/session/provider-google ok; go test ./... green except pre-existing TestProviderToolsCLIContract (re-verified at HEAD with changes stashed); vet clean; gofmt clean on changed/added files.
